question: Does the rejected whole-episode preference student alter direct-policy choices on shared-prefix states where exact teacher and source actions were identical, or is its drift localized to teacher-source divergence?
sample: Use every terminal outcome-discordant pair from the already-inspected 128-map fit window seed6561000. Never query reserved calibration, offline-validation, game or final windows. The frozen source and rejected student checkpoint hashes are fixed before this audit.
measurements: For each pair, compare exact acting-seat/action-index traces until the first divergence. Replay both complete games. On root-seat decisions in the shared prefix, teacher-branch remainder and source-branch remainder, compare saved action with frozen-source and rejected-student argmax, and measure frozen-source-to-student action KL. Verify source argmax equals each saved source-selfplay action. Summarize teacher-preferred and source-preferred pairs separately. The shared prefix is defined by exact recorded actions, not similar coarse states.
interpretation_limits: The fit games trained this rejected student. These measurements can localize policy drift but cannot establish a causal contribution, held-out generalization, autonomous strength, an acceptable KL threshold, Elo or a deployable student. Do not tune the rejected checkpoint, protocol beta/LR/epochs, offline gate or old seeds from this audit.
compute: Read-only fit replay on SSH server fedora-toolbox scratch, one CPU15 pinned nice19 with Rayon/BLAS one thread, no GPU or parallel heavy job; bounded aggregate output.
